success_criteria.description: All five districts are in use and every precinct is assigned.
All five districts have roughly equal population (within 5%).
No district may be a thin strip or a sprawling tentacle — every district must be reasonably compact (compactness ≥ 42%).
At least one district must be an effective Latino majority (≥ 50% of population) — and, like every district, it must be compact.

character.name: You
character.motivation: A federal court has struck Vera County's map. One district had concentrated the county's Latino community far past a majority, in a shape so irregular the court held that race predominated over traditional districting principles. Your task is to draw a lawful map — one that still gives the community a fair opportunity to elect its candidate of choice.

intro_slides.body:
Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act can require a majority-minority district. Under Thornburg v. Gingles (1986), where a minority community is large and compact enough to form a district majority, votes cohesively, and is usually outvoted by a bloc majority, a map that denies it that district may dilute its votes.

Vera County's Latino community, along the southern coast, meets that description. It is entitled to a district it can elect.
intro_slides.heading: When the Law Requires a District

intro_slides.body:
The Constitution limits how such a district may be drawn. When race predominates over traditional principles and the district is not reasonably compact, courts apply strict scrutiny (Shaw v. Reno; Miller v. Johnson; Bethune-Hill v. Virginia).

The old map packed the community well past a bare majority into a thin, winding shape. That is what the court struck — not the majority-minority district itself, but its form.
intro_slides.heading: But There Is a Ceiling

intro_slides.body:
This scenario uses simplified data. It measures each district's Latino population share — real Voting Rights Act analysis uses voting-age population and asks a harder question this game does not model: whether the community can actually elect its candidate of choice, given who turns out and how people vote.

A real court also weighs intent alongside shape. Here, the compactness score stands in for that judgment — but a district does not have to look bizarre to be a racial gerrymander. Courts weigh intent and process, not shape alone; this scenario uses shape as the part you can see. What is faithful is the shape of the tradeoff, not the exact numbers.
intro_slides.heading: What This Map Can and Can't Show

intro_slides.body:
A district only needs 50% + 1 to be an effective majority (Bartlett v. Strickland). You do not need to pack it higher, and you may not draw it as a tentacle to do so.

Draw a map where the Latino community holds one COMPACT majority district. Keep all five districts compact, contiguous, and balanced in population.
intro_slides.heading: Your Task

narrative.objective: Draw a compact, population-balanced map with at least one compact district where Latino voters are a majority (≥ 50%).
